from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        x_line = DashedLine(axes.c2p(0, 0), axes.c2p(3, 0), color=RED)

        self.play(Create(x_line), Create(y_line))
        self.lecture[3].set_color(ORANGE)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(vector.animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Vector Addition: The Head-to-Tail Rule", [
            "Vector addition combines two distinct movements together.",
            "Walk the first path, then the second path.",
            "Start the second path at the first's tip.",
            "Example: 2 East, 3 North, then 1 East, 1 North.",
            "The result is a new vector: (3, 4)."
        ])

        # Define vectors
        v = Vector([2, 3], color="#00FFFF")
        w = Vector([1, 1], color="#00FFFF")
        origin = ORIGIN
        
        # Grid area for visual
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 4, 1], axis_config={"include_numbers": False}).scale(0.5)
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.6)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display two vectors 'v' and 'w' in color #00FFFF.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        v.shift(axes.c2p(0, 0) - v.get_start())
        w.shift(axes.c2p(0, 0) - w.get_start())
        self.play(Create(v), Create(w))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Walk the first path, then the second path.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Start the second path at the first's tip.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.play(w.animate.shift(axes.c2p(2, 3) - w.get_start()))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Example: 2 East, 3 North, then 1 East, 1 North.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # The result is a new vector: (3, 4).
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        result = Vector([3, 4], color="#FFFF00")
        result.shift(axes.c2p(0, 0) - result.get_start())
        self.play(Create(result))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Conclusion", [
            "Vectors represent motion; addition combines these paths.",
            "Scalars scale motion; basis vectors define our coordinates.",
            "Think of GPS: adding vectors for precise navigation."
        ])
        
        # Animations
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FF6F61"))
        text1 = MathTex(r"v + w = \text{resultant path}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(text1, 'B2', 'B5')
        self.play(FadeIn(text1))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE),
                  self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#6B5B95"))
        text2 = MathTex(r"c \cdot v = \text{scaled motion}", color=WHITE)
        self.place_in_area(text2, 'C2', 'C5')
        self.play(FadeIn(text2))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE),
                  self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#88B04B"))
        # Using a simple dot as placeholder for GPS asset
        gps_dot = Dot(color="#88B04B")
        self.place_at_grid(gps_dot, 'D3')
        self.play(FadeIn(gps_dot), Write(Text("GPS Target", font_size=18).next_to(gps_dot, RIGHT)))

        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(text1), FadeOut(text2), FadeOut(gps_dot), FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title))

outline.topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: Vectors as Arrows
outline.target_audience: High school students and introductory computer science learners

sections.title: Introduction: What is a Vector?
sections.content: Define a vector not just as a list of numbers, but as a directed segment in 2D space. Explain the 'origin' and 'tip' to help visualize movement.
sections.example: Visualize a robotic arm at the origin (0,0) reaching out to a coordinate (3,2). The vector is the arrow connecting the start to the target.

sections.title: Vector Addition: The Head-to-Tail Rule
sections.content: Introduce vector addition geometrically. Explain that adding two vectors is equivalent to 'walking' the first path, then starting the second path from the end of the first.
sections.example: A cat walks 2 steps East and 3 steps North. Then, it walks another 1 step East and 1 step North. Use a coordinate grid to show the resulting final position (3,4).

sections.title: Scalar Multiplication: Stretching and Flipping
sections.content: Explain how multiplying a vector by a constant (scalar) changes its length. Discuss how negative scalars flip the direction entirely.
sections.example: A video game character jumping: A vector represents the jump strength. Doubling the vector (scalar 2) makes the character jump twice as high; multiplying by -1 makes the character jump downwards.

sections.title: Basis Vectors: The Building Blocks
sections.content: Introduce 'i-hat' (1,0) and 'j-hat' (0,1) as the fundamental basis. Explain that every vector is just a scaled combination of these two pillars.
sections.example: Using Lego bricks: Think of 'i-hat' as a red brick and 'j-hat' as a blue brick. Any coordinate (x, y) is simply x red bricks and y blue bricks stacked together.

sections.title: Summary and Conclusion
sections.content: Synthesize the concepts: Vectors are movements, addition is combining paths, scalars are scaling, and basis vectors are the coordinate system's DNA.
sections.example: Briefly show a navigation app on a phone: '2 miles North, 1 mile East' is effectively a vector addition problem used in real-time GPS tracking.
